title: Base change and finite-stage unramifiedness of a first-Fitting subscheme
statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty directed set and $(S_i)_{i\in I}$ an inverse system of affine schemes, each isomorphic to the spectrum of a commutative ring [def-weil-affine-spectrum] of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with affine transition morphisms [pqf-def-affine-morphism] and limit $S$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. Fix $c\in I$ and a finitely presented morphism $g_c:X_c\to S_c$ of schemes [def-pc-scheme], where finite presentation means locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. For $i\ge c$ write $g_i:X_i=X_c\times_{S_c}S_i\to S_i$ and write $h:X=X_c\times_{S_c}S\to S$ for the limit base change [def-pc-fibre-product]. Define $Z_c=\operatorname{Sing}(g_c)$, $Z_i=\operatorname{Sing}(g_i)$ and $Z=\operatorname{Sing}(h)$ as the closed subschemes cut out by the first Fitting ideals of the respective sheaves of relative differentials [def-trf-first-fitting-singular-subscheme]. For every morphism $T\to S_c$, the first-Fitting subscheme of $X_c\times_{S_c}T\to T$ is canonically $Z_c\times_{S_c}T$ as a closed subscheme of $X_c\times_{S_c}T$. In particular $Z_i\cong Z_c\times_{S_c}S_i$ and $Z\cong Z_c\times_{S_c}S$. Each $Z_i$ is of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ and is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and $Z_c\to S_c$ is locally of finite type. If $Z\to S$ is unramified [def-weil-unramified-morphism], then there exists $d\ge c$ such that $Z_d\to S_d$ is unramified. No flatness or nodality hypothesis on $g_c$ or $h$ is imposed.

proof.text: Finite presentation of $g_c$ gives local finite type: a finitely presented algebra is generated by the images of its finitely many polynomial variables. Together with the assumed quasi-compactness this makes $g_c$ finite type. By finite-type base change, every $g_i$ and $h$, and also $X_c\times_{S_c}T\to T$ for arbitrary $T\to S_c$, is finite type. The affine bases $S_i$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated.

proof.text: Fix any $T\to S_c$, and put $X_T=X_c\times_{S_c}T$ with projection $p:X_T\to X_c$. Relative differential base change gives the canonical isomorphism $p^*\Omega^1_{X_c/S_c}\cong\Omega^1_{X_T/T}$. The differential sheaves are finite-type quasi-coherent modules, since $g_c$ is locally of finite type. Thus the hypotheses of Fitting-ideal sheaf pullback are satisfied even when $T\to S_c$ is not flat.

Apply Fitting-ideal sheaf pullback with $r=1$ to the differential sheaf in step 2. The first Fitting ideal on $X_T$ is the image ideal $p^{-1}\operatorname{Fit}_1(\Omega^1_{X_c/S_c})\mathcal O_{X_T}$, and its closed subscheme is $X_T\times_{X_c}Z_c$. By the fibre-product universal property this is $Z_c\times_{S_c}T$: maps to either side are precisely maps to $Z_c$ and $T$ with equal composites to $S_c$. Both identifications preserve the map into $X_T$, hence give the required canonical identification as closed subschemes. Specialize to $T=S_i$ and $T=S$.

Each closed immersion $Z_i\hookrightarrow X_i$ is finite type directly from the affine quotient description: above $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset X_i$ it is $\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)\to\operatorname{Spec}A$. Its source is quasi-compact because it is affine, and $A/J$ is generated as an $A$-algebra by the empty family. These affine tests give quasi-compactness and local finite type, hence finite type. This includes $i=c$.

For every $i\ge c$, compose the finite-type morphisms $Z_i\to X_i$, $g_i:X_i\to S_i$ and the assumed finite-type structure morphism $S_i\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. Finite-type composition shows that $Z_i$ is finite type over $\mathbf Z$, and that $Z_c\to S_c$ is finite type, in particular locally of finite type. Finite type over $\mathbf Z$ makes $Z_i$ Noetherian, which includes quasi-compactness; a locally Noetherian scheme is quasi-separated. Thus $Z_i$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, especially at $c$.

Assume $Z\to S$ is unramified. Apply unramified limit descent with initial index $c$, $U_0=Z_c$, $V_0=S_c$ and $g_0:Z_c\to S_c$ its structure morphism. The bases are qcqs and transitions affine by step 1 and the hypotheses; $U_0,V_0$ are qcqs by steps 1 and 5; $g_0$ is locally of finite type by step 5. Step 3 identifies its limit base change with $Z\to S$ and its stage base changes with $Z_i\to S_i$. Restricting indices to $i\ge c$ preserves the limit: this tail is directed and cofinal, since any $i$ has a common upper bound with $c$; a compatible cone on the tail extends uniquely to $i$ using any such upper bound, independently of that choice by directedness. The descent lemma therefore gives $d\ge c$ with $Z_d\to S_d$ unramified. None of these applications requires flatness or nodality.
